title: Leak comparison at constant volume velocity (theory-only example)
description: Four identical 30 cm3 cavities (with their thermal wall loss), each driven by its own 1 cm3/s volume-velocity source, differing only in their leak to ambient (spec Appendix C3). Sealed: p/U = 1/(j w C) falls 6 dB per octave. Resistive: the spec's 0.2 mm x 30 mm x 10 mm slit, Poiseuille corner 1/(2 pi R C) = 83 Hz, -3 dB near 73 Hz and a 0.8 dB bump, no resonance (errata E45). Inertive: the spec's 1 mm x 30 mm x 10 mm slit, inertive above about 24 Hz, Helmholtz peak near 523 Hz with Q about 9, far below the Poiseuille estimate because its resistance grows with the square root of frequency. Vent: a 2 mm x 10 mm tube with a flanged inner end and an unflanged outer end, a Helmholtz resonator at about 154 Hz with Q about 5 (165 Hz lossless: the viscous boundary layer adds mass). Relative to the sealed cavity each response is H = Z_L/(Z_L + 1/(j w C)).
